messages:
kai: quick dump from the regional sweep — streaming (SSE) vs websocket vs plain HTTP polling across GPU families (A100, L40, H100) and two regions (us-west, eu-central). TL;dr: SSE lowers tail for short requests, websocket wins for sustained batched long sequences. attaching micro-table + snippets.

maria: awesome. can you paste the exact bench flags you used? need to reproduce quant/kv-cache behavior.

kai: sure — run from perf runner:```./bench --model redwood-v2-7b --mode={sse,ws,poll} --seq_len=64,512 --batch=1,8 --gpu=A100,L40,H100 --region=us-west,eu-central --kv_cache=on --quant=fp16```

tyler: network note: eu-central showed +8-12ms infra latency vs us-west during the run window (noisy host). that explains some p50 shift for websocket.

maria: can you paste the CSV? small table enough.

kai: pasted below (p95,p99 in ms, throughput in tokens/s)

```csv
mode,gpu,region,seq,batch,p95_ms,p99_ms,tokens_per_s
SSE,A100,us-west,64,1,18,40,12500
WS,A100,us-west,64,8,24,85,24000
POLL,A100,us-west,64,1,30,130,9000
SSE,L40,eu-central,512,1,85,210,4200
WS,L40,eu-central,512,8,110,350,9800
WS,H100,us-west,512,8,62,170,15000
SSE,H100,us-west,64,1,14,32,16000
```

sasha: interesting that SSE p99 bounces to 210ms on L40/512. is that kernel selection (fused-attn vs matmul) or driver?

maria: looked at logs — when seq>=256 on L40 the runtime picks fallback GEMM kernels (no fused attn) which kills p99. also kv-cache growth hits memory churn more on L40.

kai: here's the quick kernel mapping we saw in traces: `fused_attention` used on H100/A100 for seq<=256, `bmm_gemm` fallback on L40+longseq. caused extra memcpy + small-kernel overhead.

perf-bot: auto-summary: "SSE reduces p99 for short seqs by ~20-30% on A100/H100; WS higher throughput for batched long seqs; L40 shows kernel fallback for long seqs causing p99 regressions. Recommend: per-region runtime config to prefer WS for sustained batched workloads in eu-central; force kernel-path hint for L40 (if acceptable) to avoid fallback for seq in [256,512]."

tyler: follow-ups: 1) add an automated check in model onboarding to detect kernel fallback w/ seq distribution. 2) add a regional autoscale policy tweak for ws-heavy endpoints in eu-central.

maria: also try quant=4bit test next — may amplify kernel fallback due to different kernel availability. I'll spin that up tomorrow.

sasha: client side: recommend keep-alive 30s and smaller websocket frames when using ws for throughput to avoid head-of-line stalls.

kai: putting a short action list: - maria: run quant-4bit + same sweep (due by EOD tomorrow) - tyler: add a perf alert rule for kernel-fallback rate >1% - sasha: add client keepalive guidance doc snippet - infra: check eu-central host noise window and mark noisy racks.

deploy-bot: scheduled job created: `perf/sweeps/2123456789-edge-vs-core` (start: 2026-03-21T09:00Z)

maria: thanks — will post updated CSV + small plots when done. :rocket:

kai: cheers, that should help decisions on routing policy (latency-first vs cost-first) per endpoint. :+1:
